title: Does a new coolant cool enough to pay?
intro:
A machine shop is testing a new cutting coolant. It costs more, and the tooling engineer worked out that it pays only if it lowers the mean tool-tip temperature by **more than 3 °C**. Separate cuts were measured with each coolant. Old coolant: n₁ = 14 cuts, mean 413.8 °C, standard deviation 6.8 °C. New coolant: n₂ = 12 cuts, mean 405.1 °C, standard deviation 5.9 °C. The decision rule was set before the trial: switch only if a one-sided **Welch** test at α = 0.05 shows μ₁ − μ₂ > 3, that is, H₀: μ₁ − μ₂ = 3 against H₁: μ₁ − μ₂ > 3.

Find the t statistic and the one-sided p-value. Give t to two decimals and p to four decimals or more. Then apply the decision rule: does the trial say to switch?

To use the Workbench: press Ctrl+B and choose **Two-sample test**. Set **Test** to *Two means, unequal variances (Welch t)*, **Data from** to *Summary statistics entered here*, **Alternative hypothesis** to *Greater than (>)*, **Significance level (α)** to 0.05 and **Hypothesized difference (Δ₀)** to 3, then type the old coolant as sample 1 and the new one as sample 2: **Sample 1 mean (x̄₁)** = 413.8, **Sample 1 standard deviation (s₁)** = 6.8, **Sample 1 size (n₁)** = 14, **Sample 2 mean (x̄₂)** = 405.1, **Sample 2 standard deviation (s₂)** = 5.9 and **Sample 2 size (n₂)** = 12. Ctrl+L brings you back.

Statistic.says: That t tests a difference of 0. The question is whether the cut is more than 3 °C: subtract Δ₀ = 3 from x̄₁ − x̄₂ before dividing by the SE.
That is the pooled t. The decision rule says Welch: SE = √(s₁²/n₁ + s₂²/n₂).
The coolants are swapped: the old coolant is sample 1, so x̄₁ − x̄₂ = +8.7 before subtracting Δ₀ = 3.
Check the sign and the order: t = (x̄₁ − x̄₂ − Δ₀)/SE with the old coolant first. The old coolant runs hotter, so x̄₁ − x̄₂ is positive.

PValue.says: That is a two-sided p-value. H₁ is one-sided (>): p = P(T > t), one tail.
That is the pooled test's p-value. The decision rule says Welch, with ν from the Welch–Satterthwaite formula.
That p-value tests a difference of 0. The decision needs the test against Δ₀ = 3.

hints: With the old coolant as sample 1, the observed difference is x̄₁ − x̄₂, and H₀ says it is Δ₀ = 3.
SE = √(s₁²/n₁ + s₂²/n₂) and t = (x̄₁ − x̄₂ − 3)/SE. ν = (a + b)²/(a²/(n₁ − 1) + b²/(n₂ − 1)) with a = s₁²/n₁ and b = s₂²/n₂.
One-sided (>): p = P(T > t). Python stats.t.sf(t, nu), R pt(t, nu, lower.tail = FALSE).
The decision: if p is below α = 0.05, the trial shows the cut is more than 3 °C, and the rule says switch to the new coolant; if not, keep the old one.
